ceilings.note: The headline surface: what a psu Claude ENGINEER session pays in prose before its first turn. Contains the base playbook, the Claude overlay, the generated sections, the compaction protocol and the whole project guide, so lowering any component below lowers this too. Floor 120000 is set just under a render that lost the project guide (~132000 B measured 2026-09-18) so that collapse is caught by the floor as well as by the composition probe.
ceilings.ceilingRaised: 2026-09-28 RATCHET (EI-24511252962859723): 254200 -> 249800. The durable fix for the mitigation below: three guide parts trimmed by 4,014 B, with their case history moved to #evidence prose parts that do not project. Measured 248,839 B after the trim. The residual ~3.8 KB over the pre-freeze 245000 is the gate/pipeline rules the guide genuinely gained after 09-18, kept for that stated reason. EARLIER: 2026-09-28: 245000 -> 254200. TEMPORARY MITIGATION (WI-10003582) because this leg red-pinned the frozen gate lineage (candidate ac857b4b) for its whole life: the project guide it embeds grew ~6.1 KB of gate/pipeline rules between 09-18 and the freeze, and a part-by-part trim on a frozen lineage risks deleting doc-claims-pinned rules (the 09-18 regression below). Durable fix = relocate evidence-heavy guide parts to the corpus with the doc-claims suite as the guard, then ratchet this back down; tracked as EI-24511252962859723. PRIOR: 2026-09-18: 244000 -> 245000. NOT growth — a REGRESSION REPAIR (WI-10001827). The 244000 ratchet was taken while the guide was missing rules that seven doc-claims pin: the P-005 compression campaign deleted them, the byte gate measures bytes only, and nothing in the loop ran the doc-claims suite, so the ratchet recorded a number that was never legitimate. It measured a BROKEN file. Restoring the deleted rules (recovered verbatim from git, not re-invented) put the suite back to 74/74 files and 756/756 tests, and the ceiling has to follow the corrected content rather than pin the damage in place. Ratcheting a shrink-only budget onto content no independent check has validated is the anti-pattern this note exists to flag.

ceilings.note: The projected CLAUDE.md spliced into every su render. GENERATED from harness_shared.harness_doc_parts — to reduce it, edit the PART and re-project (npm run set-doc-part / node scripts/project-doc-parts.mjs --write); never hand-edit the file. The projector already enforces PROJECTION_BUDGET_CHARS=160000 by DROPPING low-priority parts, which is a catastrophe floor, not a ratchet: this ceiling fails loudly at the current size instead of letting the document grow ~38000 chars into that headroom and start silently deleting guidance.

ceilings.note: The SECOND projection of the SAME harness_doc_parts, for codex clients. Governed separately from CLAUDE.md because the reader threshold differs sharply: the projector reports this file as OVER an 80,000-char warn threshold by ~40,000, which CLAUDE.md is not measured against — so reducing the parts is worth more here than the shared ceiling suggests. It moves in lockstep with project-guide:claude-md (same parts, different client scope), so a part edit changes BOTH; that is why it is declared rather than folded into one ceiling. Found only because the guard REFUSED it as `unbaselined` after a re-projection surfaced it.

ceilings.note: The rendered compaction floor (papercusp-compaction.base.md + the client overlay) that every Claude session carries. Rendered through the SAME renderCompactionStrategy the install flow uses, so this cannot drift from what agents receive.
The authored engineer base playbook — the file a person actually edits, capped separately from the render so growth is ATTRIBUTABLE to the prose rather than to a component further down the chain.
The authored power base playbook. Same attribution rationale as su-base:engineer.

The three per-client tooling overlays (claude, codex, omp) summed. One ceiling over the sum rather than three: each is small, they grow for the same reasons, and a single total still catches growth in any one of them. Only one overlay is spliced per launch, so this is a governance bound on the authored set, not a per-session cost.
